key_insight: A tighter reduction from quantum Fourier transforms (QFTs) to integer multiplication removes one logarithmic factor from prior exact and approximate QFT gate bounds.
engineering_relevance: Lower QFT gate counts could reduce logical circuit costs for phase estimation and Shor-style algorithms, though hardware-level savings remain unestablished.
method: Use multiplication circuits with O(n(log n)^α) gates to construct exact QFT circuits with O(q(log q)^α) gates.
Obtain an exact QFT gate bound of O(q log q), improving the cited O(q(log q)^2 log log q) bound.
Reduce approximate QFT gate complexity to O(q(log log(q/ε))^α), removing one exponent from the prior bound.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical circuit-size bounds and comparisons with prior constructions, not experimental benchmarks or hardware evaluations.
watch_item: Practical gains depend on multiplication-circuit costs, gate synthesis, and hardware constraints; sub-O(q log q) scaling is presented only as a conditional possibility.
paper_title: Improved Exact and Approximate Quantum Fourier Transforms from Multiplication
